items.followUp: Describe how Biology is related to Biochemistry and Bioinformatics.

rubric.why: Biophysics applies physics to biological systems and processes.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between Biology and Biophysics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for stating that Biophysics uses the principles or methods of physics to study living organisms or biological processes.

rubric.why: Biomathematics uses mathematical or statistical methods to investigate biological questions.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between Biology and Biomathematics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for explaining that mathematical or statistical methods are applied to biological problems or data.

rubric.why: A suitable application illustrates how mathematics can be used to investigate biological questions.
rubric.description: Gives an example of an application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as using mathematical models to study population growth.

modelAnswer: Biophysics is the application of the principles and methods of physics to the study of living organisms and their processes.
It helps explain biological phenomena using physical laws and techniques.
Biomathematics applies mathematical and statistical methods to biological problems and data.
For example, mathematical models can be used to study population growth.
Thus, both fields use other disciplines to investigate biological questions.

items.followUp: Compare the functions of skeletal and cardiac muscles.

rubric.why: Skeletal muscle is typically attached to bones and works under voluntary control.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying skeletal muscle and a correct feature such as its attachment to bones or voluntary control.

rubric.why: Smooth muscle occurs in internal organs and works involuntarily.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying smooth muscle and a correct feature such as its spindle-shaped cells, location or involuntary action.

rubric.why: Cardiac muscle is found in the heart and contracts involuntarily.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cardiac muscle and a correct feature such as its location, branched fibres or involuntary action.

rubric.why: A structural feature or location provides a valid distinction between the muscle tissue types.
rubric.description: Gives an additional distinguishing feature or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct additional structural feature or location, such as spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells, branched cardiac fibres or skeletal muscles attached to bones.

modelAnswer: Skeletal (striated) muscle has long fibres, is usually attached to bones and works voluntarily.
Smooth (unstriated) muscle has spindle-shaped cells, occurs in the walls of internal organs and works involuntarily.
Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart; its branched, striated fibres contract involuntarily.
Thus, the three muscle tissues differ in structure, location and control.

items.followUp: Describe two uses of enzymes in industry or medicine.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts, and their catalytic action supports their many uses.
rubric.description: States the catalytic role of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes act as biological catalysts or speed up chemical reactions.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used in food production and processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid food-industry application, such as cheese-making or bread-making.

rubric.why: Enzymes in detergents help break down stains and clean clothes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that enzymes help detergents remove stains or clean clothes.

rubric.why: Enzymes also have medical applications and are used in material-processing industries.
rubric.description: Gives medical and other industrial uses.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for mentioning both a valid medical use and a valid industrial use, such as diagnostic tests or treatments and leather, textile or paper processing.

modelAnswer: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and are used in many fields.
In the food industry, they are used in processes such as cheese-making and bread-making.
Enzymes in detergents break down stains and help clean clothes.
In medicine, enzymes are used in diagnostic tests and some treatments.
They are also used in industries such as leather, textile and paper processing.

items.followUp: Name one product obtained through agriculture and state its importance.

rubric.why: Agriculture involves cultivating crops and raising useful animals.
rubric.description: Describes the work involved in agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing agriculture as crop cultivation and/or the raising of useful animals.

rubric.why: Agriculture supplies food and useful materials for people and industry.
rubric.description: States the importance or products of agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that agriculture supplies food, fibres, raw materials or other useful products.

modelAnswer: Agriculture is the profession and practice of cultivating crops and raising useful animals.
It supplies food and useful products such as fibres and other raw materials.
